name: Melee Weapons & Armor
description: Questions covering: Swords, Polearms, Armor Materials, Blunt Weapons, Ancient Spears. Test your knowledge in this category.

questions.question: Which Japanese curved blade is known by this name?
questions.explanation_correct: A katana is the classic Japanese curved sword associated with samurai. It is distinct from other Japanese edged weapons by its length and single-edged blade.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are different Japanese weapons or sword types, not the specific curved blade named here.

questions.question: Which Swiss infantry polearm is described here?
questions.explanation_correct: A halberd is a combined axe-and-spear pole weapon historically used by infantry. It was especially prominent in Swiss and German military traditions.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are pole weapons too, but they are not the Swiss infantry weapon in question.

questions.question: What term refers to protective armor made of interlinked rings?
questions.explanation_correct: Chainmail is armor constructed from many interlinked metal rings. It was widely used for flexible body protection.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are different armor constructions and do not use linked rings as their defining feature.

questions.question: Which spiked-headed club is being described?
questions.explanation_correct: A mace is a blunt weapon with a heavy head that may be spiked. It is designed to deliver crushing strikes.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are related melee weapons, but they are not the specific spiked-headed club named here.

questions.question: Which Greek long spear was used by ancient infantry formations?
questions.explanation_correct: The sarissa was the exceptionally long spear used by Macedonian phalanxes. Its length allowed dense spear walls in formation fighting.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are either different spear types or non-spear weapons from antiquity.

questions.question: Which Roman rectangular shield is this?
questions.explanation_correct: The scutum was the large rectangular shield carried by Roman soldiers. It is one of the most recognizable Roman shield forms.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are shield types too, but they are not the Roman rectangular shield referenced here.

questions.question: Which single-handed throwing axe fits this description?
questions.explanation_correct: The francisca was a Frankish throwing axe used in warfare. It was small enough to be thrown effectively with one hand.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are axes or axe-like tools, but they are not the specific historical throwing axe named here.

questions.question: Which Indian punch dagger is described here?
questions.explanation_correct: A katar is an Indian thrusting dagger with a distinctive H-shaped grip. It is designed for punching-style stabs.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are blades or knives, but they are not the Indian punch dagger in question.

questions.question: Which ancient Greek helmet style is famous for its large eye slits and fixed nose guard?
questions.explanation_correct: The Corinthian style offered great protection but impaired hearing and vision significantly.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Boeotian and Phrygian helmets usually left the face open for better situational awareness.

questions.question: Which armored hand covering is described here?
questions.explanation_correct: A gauntlet is a protective armored glove or hand covering. It was commonly used as part of plate armor.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are armor pieces too, but they protect other body parts rather than the hand.

questions.question: Which mounted combat weapon is designed for a cavalry charge and thrusting from horseback?
questions.explanation_correct: A lance is the classic cavalry weapon used for thrusting during a mounted charge. It is built for reach and impact from horseback.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are polearms or spears not specifically defined by cavalry charge use. They are not the standard mounted thrusting weapon.

questions.question: Which Japanese polearm features a blade mounted along a shaft?
questions.explanation_correct: A naginata is a Japanese polearm with a curved blade attached to a shaft. It was used for sweeping and cutting attacks.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are either different Japanese polearms or generic spears. They do not specifically describe the blade-on-shaft design of a naginata.

questions.question: Which medieval sword is known for its large two-handed form?
questions.explanation_correct: A zweihander is a very large sword intended for two-handed use. It is associated with late medieval and Renaissance warfare.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are smaller or differently shaped swords. They are not the large two-handed type described here.

questions.question: Which armor component protects the neck with a plate-like piece?
questions.explanation_correct: A gorget is an armor piece that protects the throat and neck. It often sits around the base of the neck.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options protect different parts of the body, such as shoulders, torso, or hands. They are not neck-protecting plates.

questions.question: What siege-defense material was used as a heated alternative to pouring liquids on attackers?
questions.explanation_correct: Hot sand was sometimes used in defense of fortifications as a burning or scalding deterrent. It could be poured on attackers in place of liquids.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are materials, but they are not the specific substitute described. Hot sand is the intended answer.

questions.question: Which ancient Greek short sword was commonly carried by infantry?
questions.explanation_correct: The xiphos was a short, straight sword used in ancient Greece. It was a common sidearm for hoplites.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are swords from different traditions or forms. They are not the specific Greek short sword named here.

questions.question: Which medieval infantry spear was especially associated with very long reach formations?
questions.explanation_correct: A pike is a very long thrusting spear used by infantry in dense formations. It was designed for reach and battlefield control.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are shorter throwing or thrusting weapons, or different polearms. They are not the long infantry spear indicated here.

questions.question: Which single-handed Viking axe is characterized by a hooked lower blade edge?
questions.explanation_correct: A bearded axe has an extended lower blade that resembles a beard. This shape gives it a distinctive grip and cutting profile.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are axes or throwing axes, but they do not match the distinctive hooked-blade form. They are not the single-handed Viking bearded axe.

questions.question: Which Scottish companion dagger has a basket hilt style of protection?
questions.explanation_correct: The dirk is a Scottish dagger associated with side carry and companion use. In this context, it refers to the traditional Scottish dagger form.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are daggers or knife types, but not the one identified by this Scottish companion-dagger description. They do not match the target term.

questions.question: Which Japanese studded war club is known for its iron or metal protrusions?
questions.explanation_correct: A kanabo is a Japanese war club often reinforced with metal studs or spikes. It is associated with heavy crushing blows.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are generic clubs or different weapons. They are not the studded Japanese war club specified here.

questions.question: Which armor piece is a rigid torso defense made of metal plates?
questions.explanation_correct: A cuirass is a body armor piece designed to protect the torso, typically formed of front and back metal plates. It is distinct from limb armor and mail garments.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A hauberk is a mail shirt, while greaves and pauldrons protect the legs and shoulders, not the torso.

questions.question: Which medieval helmet has a pointed top and a nasal guard?
questions.explanation_correct: A spangenhelm is a segmented medieval helmet often characterized by a pointed crown and a nasal guard. It was widely used in early medieval Europe.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A bascinet, great helm, and sallet are different helmet forms without that characteristic segmented pointed structure.

questions.question: Which small round shield was often used in fist fighting?
questions.explanation_correct: A buckler is a small round shield designed for close combat and weapon deflection. It is commonly associated with sword-and-buckler fighting.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A tower shield, kite shield, and target are larger shield types with different uses and shapes.

questions.question: Which curved cavalry sword originated in the Middle East?
questions.explanation_correct: A scimitar is a curved single-edged sword associated with cavalry and Middle Eastern weapon traditions. Its distinctive curve sets it apart from straight swords.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A rapier, falchion, and longsword are different sword forms, typically straighter or differently shaped and used.

questions.question: Which Japanese spear was used by samurai?
questions.explanation_correct: A yari is a Japanese spear used in warfare by samurai and ashigaru. It is a straight thrusting polearm rather than a bladed pole weapon.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A naginata is a pole weapon with a curved blade, while a halberd and partisan are non-Japanese polearms of different forms.

questions.question: Which Italian Renaissance dagger is made for stabbing?
questions.explanation_correct: A stiletto is a slim dagger designed primarily for thrusting and piercing. It is especially associated with Italian Renaissance weaponry.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A dirk, main-gauche, and kris are different dagger types with other shapes, origins, or intended uses.

questions.question: Which padded defensive jacket was worn under armor?
questions.explanation_correct: A gambeson is a quilted padded garment worn as armor or beneath other armor to absorb impact. It served as both standalone protection and underlayer.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A brigandine, cuirass, and hauberk are different armor forms made of plates or mail rather than padded cloth.

questions.question: Which Japanese helmet was worn by samurai?
questions.explanation_correct: A kabuto is the traditional Japanese helmet worn by samurai. It often features a prominent crest and complex construction.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A morion, sallet, and bascinet are European helmet types, not Japanese samurai helmets.

questions.question: Which large shield was used by crossbowmen to provide cover?
questions.explanation_correct: A pavise is a large shield used to protect missile troops, especially crossbowmen, during reloading. It was often set on the ground for cover.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A buckler, heater shield, and targe are smaller or differently shaped shields not typically used as standing cover for crossbowmen.

questions.question: Which long-shafted Danish war axe was common in medieval warfare?
questions.explanation_correct: The Dane axe is a long-handled battle axe associated with Viking and early medieval warfare. It is known for its broad blade and two-handed use.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A bearded axe, francisca, and pollaxe are different axe types with different blade shapes, sizes, or combat roles.

questions.question: Which term refers to a Roman short sword?
questions.explanation_correct: A gladius was the standard short sword used by Roman infantry. It is one of the most recognizable weapons of the Roman military.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are different weapon types or traditions: a Nepalese blade, an axe, and a polearm.

questions.question: Which term refers to a curved Nepalese blade?
questions.explanation_correct: A kukri is a distinctive Nepalese blade with a forward-curving profile. It is both a traditional tool and a weapon.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are a polearm, a dagger, and a shield, so they do not fit this description.

questions.question: Which term refers to a single-edged utility axe?
questions.explanation_correct: A tomahawk is a light axe originally associated with Native American use. It could serve as a tool or weapon.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are a blunt weapon, a flexible weapon, and a helmet rather than an axe.

questions.question: Which polearm, commonly used by English infantry, features a hooked blade derived from an agricultural tool?
questions.explanation_correct: The bill was a versatile polearm developed from the billhook, featuring a hook, a spike, and a blade.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The gladius is a short sword, the kukri is a knife, and the targe is a shield.

questions.question: Which term refers to a spear-axe combination?
questions.explanation_correct: A bardiche is a pole weapon with a long axe-like blade mounted on a shaft. It combines features of a spear and axe-like cutting edge.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are an axe, a dagger, and a flexible weapon rather than this polearm.

questions.question: Which term refers to a Scottish broad dagger?
questions.explanation_correct: A sgian-dubh is a traditional Scottish knife worn with Highland dress. It is a small dagger rather than a larger blade.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are a curved blade, a polearm, and a shield, so they do not match the description.

questions.question: Which term refers to a spiked club weapon?
questions.explanation_correct: A morgenstern, or morning star, is a club or mace-like weapon fitted with spikes. It is classified as a blunt weapon with added penetrating points.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are an axe, a polearm, and a helmet, which are not spiked clubs.

questions.question: Which term refers to a weighted chain weapon?
questions.explanation_correct: A flail is a flexible weapon made from a handle connected to one or more striking weights by a chain or strap. Its defining feature is that hinged connection.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are a polearm, a shield, and a sword, so they are not chain weapons.

questions.question: Which term refers to a small round shield?
questions.explanation_correct: A targe is a round shield associated especially with Scottish warfare. It was designed for close defense and protection.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are a blade, a spiked weapon, and a dagger, not shields.

questions.question: Which term refers to a great helm variant?
questions.explanation_correct: A bascinet is a medieval helmet that developed from earlier great helm traditions. It became a common European military helmet in the late Middle Ages.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are a flexible weapon, a polearm, and an axe, so they are not helmets.

questions.question: What is the name of the plate skirt armor worn around the hips?
questions.explanation_correct: Faulds are articulated metal plates that hang from a cuirass to protect the hips and upper thighs. They form a skirt-like section of armor.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A pauldron protects the shoulder, a vambrace protects the forearm, and a greave protects the shin. None of them are skirt-style hip armor.

questions.question: What is the name of the armored piece worn over the shoulder?
questions.explanation_correct: A pauldron is a plate armor component designed to cover and protect the shoulder. It is commonly used in medieval and Renaissance armor.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Faulds protect the hips, a vambrace covers the forearm, and a greave covers the shin. Those pieces are located on different parts of the body.

questions.question: What is the term for armor worn on the forearm?
questions.explanation_correct: A vambrace is the armor piece that protects the forearm. It often extends from the elbow toward the wrist.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A pauldron covers the shoulder, a greave covers the shin, and faulds protect the hips. None of those are forearm armor.

questions.question: What is the name of the armor worn on the shin?
questions.explanation_correct: A greave is a piece of armor that protects the shin or lower leg. It is part of leg armor used in many historical armor sets.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A vambrace protects the forearm, a pauldron protects the shoulder, and faulds protect the hips. Those are different armor locations.

questions.question: What is the Japanese staff weapon called?
questions.explanation_correct: A bō is a straight wooden staff used as a martial arts weapon. It is typically long and unbladed.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A katana is a sword, a naginata is a polearm with a blade, and a yari is a spear. They are different weapon types from a straight staff.

questions.question: What is the name of the short Japanese sword?
questions.explanation_correct: A wakizashi is a short Japanese sword traditionally worn alongside a katana. It was commonly used as a companion blade.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A katana is longer, a tanto is usually a dagger, and a nodachi is a large field sword. Those are not the standard short sword.

questions.question: Which European sword type is designed primarily for thrusting?
questions.explanation_correct: A rapier is a slender sword associated with thrusting attacks and civilian fencing. Its design emphasizes point work over heavy cutting.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A broadsword, sabre, and falchion are more strongly associated with cutting or slashing. They are not primarily thrusting swords.

questions.question: What is the Ancient Greek curved sword called?
questions.explanation_correct: The kopis is an Ancient Greek sword known for its forward-curving blade. It was effective for powerful cutting strikes.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A xiphos is a straight sword, a dory is a spear, and makhaira is a broader category of cutting blade. Those do not match the specific Greek curved sword named here.

questions.question: What is the name of a specialty spear designed to prevent a large animal from sliding up the shaft?
questions.explanation_correct: The cross-guards (lugs) on a boar spear prevented an injured animal from reaching the hunter.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Javelins are for throwing, while halberds and partisans are complex infantry weapons.

questions.question: What is the Scottish long dagger called?
questions.explanation_correct: The item intended here is the Scottish long dagger traditionally associated with Highland use. Among these options, claymore is the only one matching the required answer.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A dirk and a sgian-dubh are Scottish knives or daggers of different forms, and a bollock dagger is a distinct dagger type. Those do not match the specified target answer.

questions.question: Which term refers to a hardened leather armor made by boiling and stiffening hides?
questions.explanation_correct: Cuir bouilli is leather hardened by boiling or otherwise heat-treating it to make it stiff. It was used for armor and protective equipment.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are different armor types or materials, not boiled hardened leather. They do not name that specific treatment-based leather armor.

questions.question: Which term names a small parrying shield used in close combat?
questions.explanation_correct: Rondel refers to a small, round shield or target used for parrying in some historical contexts. It is associated with compact defensive use.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are shield types, but they are not the requested term. They belong to the same category, yet only one matches this specific name.

questions.question: What is the name of a pointed, conical helmet popular in the 11th century?
questions.explanation_correct: Often seen in the Bayeux Tapestry, it features a single iron bar covering the nose.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Bascinets and sallets appeared much later in the 14th and 15th centuries.

questions.question: Which Japanese polearm is a straight-bladed spear?
questions.explanation_correct: Hoko is a Japanese weapon described as a straight-bladed spear. It is distinct from curved-blade polearms such as the naginata.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are polearms or spear-like weapons, but they are not this specific term. They differ in blade shape or classification.

questions.question: Which Chinese weapon is known by the name for a pair of hook swords?
questions.explanation_correct: Shuang gou literally refers to paired hook swords used in Chinese martial traditions. The name identifies the hooked-blade weapon set.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are Chinese weapons, but they are not hook swords. They belong to the same general category without matching the specific name.

questions.question: Which Indian weapon is a flexible steel whip-sword?
questions.explanation_correct: Urumi is a flexible, whip-like sword from India, usually made of steel. It is notable for its thin, bendable blade.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are Indian swords or weapons, but they are not flexible whip-swords. They are different in form and use.

questions.question: What is the hand-protecting crosspiece on a sword called?
questions.explanation_correct: The guard is the crosspiece that protects the wielder's hand on a sword. It sits between the blade and the grip.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are also sword parts, but they are not the crosspiece that protects the hand. They serve different structural roles.

questions.question: What is the term for the thigh armor piece worn with plate armor?
questions.explanation_correct: A cuisse is the armor piece that protects the thigh. It was commonly part of medieval and early modern plate armor.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are armor components, but they protect different body parts. They are not the thigh plate.

questions.question: Which weapon was a long-handled wall hook used for capturing or controlling opponents?
questions.explanation_correct: A man catcher is a long-handled device with a hook or cage designed to seize a person. It was used for restraining rather than cutting or thrusting.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are pole weapons, but they are not designed primarily as catching tools. They are different offensive or utility weapons.

questions.question: Which Mesoamerican weapon is an obsidian-edged club?
questions.explanation_correct: The macuahuitl is a Mesoamerican club edged with sharp obsidian blades. It was used as a cutting weapon in pre-Columbian warfare.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are Mesoamerican terms or weapons, but they are not the obsidian-edged club. They refer to different weapon forms or unrelated words.

questions.question: Which type of European sword is known for being a hand-and-a-half blade used in medieval combat?
questions.explanation_correct: A longsword is a medieval European sword designed for versatile two-handed or hand-and-a-half use. It is distinct from shorter or more specialized blades.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are different sword types or blade forms, not the standard medieval longsword. They do not match the same weapon category or form.

questions.question: Which Japanese short companion sword was commonly worn alongside a katana?
questions.explanation_correct: A tantō is a Japanese short blade, often used as a dagger or short companion weapon. It is shorter than a wakizashi and not a pole weapon or long sword.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options include a short sword, pole weapon, and greatsword-like blade. They are not the specific short companion sword named in the question.

questions.question: Which Swiss-inspired polearm features a distinct combination of a hammer and a long spike?
questions.explanation_correct: Named after a Swiss city, this weapon was highly effective against plate armor.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The glaive and partisan are bladed weapons rather than hammers.

questions.question: Which spiked club was used in medieval Flanders?
questions.explanation_correct: A goedendag is a medieval Flemish weapon combining a club-like shaft with a spike. It is closely associated with infantry use in the Low Countries.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are blunt weapons too, but they are different forms and names. They are not the specific Flemish spiked club.

questions.question: Which ancient double-headed axe has crescent-shaped blades?
questions.explanation_correct: A labrys is a double-headed axe associated with ancient Crete and broader ancient symbolism. Its blades are typically shown in a crescent-like form.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are axes, but they are different in style, size, or historical usage. They do not match the distinctive double-headed crescent form.

questions.question: Which Roman throwing spear was designed to bend after impact?
questions.explanation_correct: A pilum was a Roman heavy javelin intended to disable shields and often bend on impact. It was a standard Roman infantry missile weapon.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are spears or spear-like weapons from different cultures or roles. They do not match the Roman heavy javelin described.

questions.question: Which European dagger is named for the distinctively shaped lobes on its hilt?
questions.explanation_correct: Popular across Europe from the 14th century, the name refers to the PH-shaped grip base.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The sgian-dubh and dirk are traditional Scottish items with different hilt constructions.

questions.question: Which small round shield is associated with Italian Renaissance fencing?
questions.explanation_correct: A rotella is a small round shield used especially in Renaissance Italy. It is specifically associated with fencing and civilian sword-and-shield combat.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are shields, but they are different shapes, sizes, or regional types. They do not match the small round Italian shield in the question.

questions.question: Which helmet variant has a face opening shaped like a frog's mouth?
questions.explanation_correct: A frog-mouth helm is a tournament-style helmet with a wide horizontal vision slit resembling a frog's mouth. It is a specific variant of the great helm.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are helmets, but they are different forms and periods. They do not match the distinctive great-helm variant described.

questions.question: Which form of body protection consists of many small plates sewn or laced to a backing?
questions.explanation_correct: Scale armor consists of overlapping plates that resemble the skin of a fish or reptile.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Mail armor is made of interlocking rings, while brigandine is riveted under cloth.

questions.question: Which term names the upper arm piece of plate armor?
questions.explanation_correct: A rerebrace is the armor worn over the upper arm, between the shoulder armor and the elbow defense. It is part of a plate harness.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options refer to different armor parts: vambrace for the forearm, cuirass for the torso, and cuisse for the thigh.

questions.question: Which term refers to the armor worn over the thigh?
questions.explanation_correct: A tasset is a piece of armor associated with the upper leg and thigh area. It is commonly used in plate armor systems.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are different armor parts: greave for the lower leg, gauntlet for the hand, and gorget for the neck.

questions.question: Which term describes a sword with a guard enclosing the hand like a cage?
questions.explanation_correct: A basket-hilt sword has a guard that surrounds and protects the wielder's hand. It is especially associated with certain European swords, such as Scottish broadswords.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are sword parts or related fittings: langets, quillon, and ricasso are not the full guarded hilt.

questions.question: Which Japanese pole weapon features a forked head used for restraining a person or horse?
questions.explanation_correct: A sasumata is a Japanese pole weapon with a forked metal head. It was traditionally used to catch, pin, or control a target.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are different Japanese pole weapons: a naginata is a curved-bladed polearm, a yari is a spear, and a bisento is a sword-like polearm.

questions.question: Which term names the armor piece that protects a horse's face?
questions.explanation_correct: A chanfron is the armored defense placed over a horse's head and face. It is part of medieval horse barding.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options protect different parts of the horse: crinet for the neck, peytral for the chest, and croupiere for the hindquarters.

questions.question: Which Japanese term refers to the shorter companion blade in a daishō pair?
questions.explanation_correct: Shōtō means the shorter sword in the daishō pairing, typically paired with a katana. It contrasts with the longer blade in the set.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are other sword types or lengths: uchigatana, nodachi, and tachi are not the specific term for the shorter companion blade.

questions.question: Which European polearm combines an axe blade, a spike, and a hook?
questions.explanation_correct: A pollaxe is a polearm designed with multiple striking features, commonly including an axe blade, a spike, and a hook. It was used in infantry combat.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are polearms too, but they do not specifically match this combination of axe, spike, and hook.

questions.question: Which term names the conical Norman helmet with a projecting nose guard?
questions.explanation_correct: A nasal helm is a medieval helmet characterized by a nasal guard protecting the face. It is commonly associated with Norman-era equipment.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are different helmet styles: great helm, barbute, and sallet do not specifically denote the Norman conical helmet with a nasal guard.

questions.question: Which Roman torso armor was made of articulated metal strips?
questions.explanation_correct: Lorica segmentata is the Roman body armor formed from segmented iron strips. It is one of the best-known types of Roman military armor.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are different Roman armor types: hamata is mail, squamata is scale armor, and plumata combines scales with mail.

questions.question: What is the term for a small, round shield held in a fist grip rather than worn on the arm?
questions.explanation_correct: Measuring between 8 and 18 inches, the buckler was used more for active parrying than static blocking.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Tower shields and scutums are much larger and strapped to the forearm.

questions.question: Which historical dagger features a hilt with two rounded lobes, popularized in Northern Europe?
questions.explanation_correct: Known also as a kidney dagger to Victorian historians, it was a common sidearm for several centuries.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The stiletto was for piercing mail, while the seax was a single-edged Germanic blade.

questions.question: Which Japanese club-like weapon was studded with metal spikes?
questions.explanation_correct: The tetsubō is a Japanese club or staff weapon sometimes described as being reinforced or studded with metal. It is associated with heavy blunt-force use.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are Japanese weapons too, but they are not the spiked club described in the blueprint.

questions.question: Which curved single-edged sword is associated with the Ottoman world?
questions.explanation_correct: The kilij is a Turkish sword form linked to the Ottoman world. It is known for its distinct curved blade.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are related curved swords, but they are not the specific Ottoman sword named in the blueprint.

questions.question: Which plate component protects the armpit gap in armor?
questions.explanation_correct: A besagew is a round plate worn to protect the armpit area in armor. It helps cover a vulnerable gap between defenses.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are armor pieces, but they protect different parts of the body rather than the armpit gap.

questions.question: Which knightly helmet is characterized by a high, pointed dome and a flat-topped appearance?
questions.explanation_correct: It evolved from the cylindrical great helm but added a pointed top to deflect strikes.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The barbute and sallet are later styles with more contoured shapes.

questions.question: Which ancient Greek cuirass was bell-shaped and named for a body part?
questions.explanation_correct: The bell cuirass is an ancient Greek bronze breastplate with a bell-like lower shape. Its name refers to that distinctive form.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are forms of ancient armor, but they are not the bell-shaped bronze cuirass specified in the blueprint.

questions.question: Which Japanese pole weapon has a straight spear-like blade and a crossbar?
questions.explanation_correct: The jumonji yari is a Japanese spear with a main blade and side crossbar blades. Its name refers to the cross-shaped arrangement.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are Japanese polearms or spears, but they do not have the crossbar design of the jumonji yari.

questions.question: What is the name for the massive infantry shields used to provide total-body coverage in battle?
questions.explanation_correct: Tower shields, like the Roman scutum, offered maximum protection for organized rank-and-file units.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The pavise was usually a freestanding shield for archers, and the buckler is very small.

questions.question: Which horseman's war hammer has a rear spike?
questions.explanation_correct: The bec de corbin is a medieval horseman's hammer with a beak-like rear spike. It was designed to concentrate force against armor.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are blunt or piercing weapons, but they are not the specific horseman's hammer with a rear spike named here.

questions.question: Which armor material is made from interlinked metal rings?
questions.explanation_correct: Mail is armor made from many interlinked metal rings. It is also called chain mail in common usage.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are armor types made in different ways, but they are not the ring-linked material described in the blueprint.

questions.question: Which term refers to the short companion sword in Japanese sword tradition?
questions.explanation_correct: Daishō is the term for the paired long and short swords carried by samurai, with the shorter one serving as the companion blade. It is a specific historical term from Japanese sword culture.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are individual Japanese sword types or a related pairing concept, but not the requested term. They do not name the short companion sword by that exact designation.

questions.question: What is the name of the Roman muscle cuirass style?
questions.explanation_correct: Lorica musculata is the Roman cuirass modeled with an idealized muscular torso. It is the standard term for this decorative body armor style.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are Roman armor types made from segments, mail, or feather-like scales. They are different constructions rather than the muscle cuirass style.

questions.question: Which term names the Japanese glaive-like weapon?
questions.explanation_correct: Bisentō is a Japanese polearm with a large blade, often described as glaive-like. It belongs to the family of bladed pole weapons.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are related Japanese weapons, but they are not the same term. They refer to a spear, a standard glaive-like polearm, or a sickle-and-chain weapon.

questions.question: Which Ottoman conical helmet is called this?
questions.explanation_correct: Çiçak is the Ottoman term for a conical helmet. It is a specific helmet form associated with Ottoman military equipment.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are helmet names from different traditions or broader helmet types. They do not match the Ottoman conical helmet term.

questions.question: What is the term for the Scottish long dagger?
questions.explanation_correct: Dudgeon refers to a long Scottish dagger, especially one associated with the Scottish tradition of dagger forms. It is the exact term requested here.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are dagger-related terms, but they do not specifically name the long Scottish dagger in the blueprint. They refer to different Scottish blades or dagger shapes.

questions.question: Which term denotes the Zulu cowhide shield?
questions.explanation_correct: Isihlangu is the large Zulu shield traditionally made from cowhide. It is the proper name for that specific shield type.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are not shields of the same type: they are a club, a spear, or a settlement enclosure. None names the Zulu cowhide shield.

questions.question: Which word names the Indian battle axe?
questions.explanation_correct: Tabar is the term for an Indian battle axe. It is a historical weapon name used in South Asian contexts.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are different Indian weapons or bladed implements, but not an axe. They refer to swords or a throwing weapon.

questions.question: Which term refers to the single-edged falchion variant?
questions.explanation_correct: Messer is a single-edged sword form often treated as a falchion-like medieval weapon. It is the requested variant name.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are sword types, but they are not the specific single-edged falchion variant named in the blueprint. They represent different blade profiles and historical usages.

questions.question: What is the name of the box-like shoulder armor in Japanese armor?
questions.explanation_correct: Sode are the large shoulder guards used in Japanese armor, often box-like in appearance. They protect the shoulders and upper arms.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are Japanese armor pieces for the torso, arms, or thighs. They are not the shoulder armor component asked for here.

questions.question: Which term refers to a knobbed wooden war club?
questions.explanation_correct: A cudgel is a short, blunt wooden club, often with a knobbed striking end. It fits the description of a knobbed wooden war club.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are blunt weapons or striking tools, but they are not the same as a simple knobbed wooden club. They differ in construction, length, or attachments.
